note: The first input byte selects one fuzzed command-line argument before the remaining bytes are written as the file under test.
The PoC supplies -t as the flac mode argument so the file payload is decoded through the normal metadata parser.
The remaining bytes are a FLAC stream beginning with fLaC and a malformed last VORBIS_COMMENT metadata block with length 3.
The metadata header is parsed from the attacker-controlled file payload; type is 4 for VORBIS_COMMENT.
The attacker-controlled metadata length is only 3 bytes, shorter than the 4-byte vendor-length field required by the VORBIS_COMMENT parser.
The short metadata length becomes a 24-bit bitreader limit for parsing the VORBIS_COMMENT contents.
VORBIS_COMMENT parsing attempts to read a 32-bit vendor length under a 24-bit limit.
The bitreader detects that the 24-bit limit is less than the requested 32-bit vendor-length read.

The limit is invalidated to UINT32_MAX on the failed read; vulnerable revisions then treated this as remaining content and continued into frame-sync recovery, allowing uninitialized buffered bytes to be consumed.
